title: The way of the elders
hookLine: the Buddhism of Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar, Laos and Cambodia, with the Pali canon as scripture

lines: A SCHOOL NAMED FOR THE ELDERS.
cards: Dawn in Luang Prabang, in Laos. A line of monks in saffron robes walks barefoot down a quiet street, bowls held in front of them. People kneel on mats by the curb and place a little sticky rice in each bowl.
No one speaks. Much the same happens in towns across Thailand, Myanmar and Cambodia, and in a different form in Sri Lanka. Tradition says it has gone on for many centuries.
After more than three weeks with the Heart Sutra and Zen, the next two go south and west, into the school that names itself for the elders.

teach.b: Theravada. Thera means an elder, a senior monk; vāda, a teaching, a way of speaking. The teaching of the elders.
The name carries a claim: this is the Buddha's teaching as the senior monks remembered and recited it after his death, kept as closely as possible ever since.
Theravada is the main Buddhism of Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar, Laos and Cambodia, with communities in Bangladesh, southern Vietnam, and cities all over the world.
Its scripture is the Pali canon, written in Pali, an ancient Indian language close to the ones the Buddha spoke. How did it get south? The Sri Lankan chronicles tell it this way.
The Indian emperor Ashoka, whose own inscriptions speak of his remorse after a bloody war, sent his son, a monk named Mahinda, to the king of Sri Lanka. The king listened and became a follower.

Ashoka's daughter, the nun Sanghamitta, came later, bringing a branch of the tree the Buddha sat under. Tradition says a tree grown from it still stands at Anuradhapura, where pilgrims honor it today.
Later, the chronicle says, monks in Sri Lanka wrote the canon down for the first time, fearing it could be lost.
From there it traveled to Southeast Asia. Theravada and Mahayana Buddhists share the core: the four truths, the eightfold path, the three refuges. Where they differ, i'll say who says what.

how: In Theravada countries monks walk an alms round at dawn, lay people offer food and visit temples on full-moon days, and the Pali canon is chanted in the original language in daily services.

games.q: match each piece of today's story.
p: Ashoka's son, sent to Sri Lanka
brought a branch of the bodhi tree

s: the Pali canon was written down first in Thailand
the chronicle says monks in Sri Lanka first wrote it down.
Theravada and Mahayana share the four truths and the eightfold path
they share the core, and differ on other points.

games.q: you're the emperor Ashoka, and you want the king of Sri Lanka to hear the Buddha's teaching. whom do you send, as the chronicles tell it?
o: an army to make sure he listens.
your own son, a monk named Mahinda.
games.why: Ashoka sent his son Mahinda, and later his daughter Sanghamitta came with a branch of the bodhi tree.

practice: Picture a map: India, the Buddha's home, then the island at its tip, Sri Lanka, then east across the sea to Myanmar, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia.
In each place, picture a line of monks at dawn and someone kneeling with a bowl of rice. Let your breath move with them, slow and quiet.
